newsitem.title: USA: U.S. discusses security in N.Iraq with Kurd leader.
newsitem.headline: U.S. discusses security in N.Iraq with Kurd leader.

text.p: A senior U.S. official discussed ways of establishing peace and security in northern Iraq at a meeting in Turkey on Wednesday with Kurdish leader Massoud Barzani, the State Department said.

Assistant Secretary of State Robert Pelletreau also discussed the humanitarian situation of Kurds and other peoples and the safety of people affiliated with U.S. operations in the region, spokesman Nicholas Burns said.

Pelletreau met Barzani, leader of the Kurdistan Democratic Perty (KDP), and a leader of the Iraqi Turkmen community at the meeting which reports from Ankara said went on for several hours at a secret location in the Turkish capital.

"They discussed continuing U.S. interest in contributing to peace and stability in the region and U.S. concerns about the humanitarian situation of the Kurds, Turkmen, Assyrians and others who live in the region, as well as concerns about the safety of those affiliated with our operations there," Burns said in a statement.

With Baghdad's help, Barzani's KDP seized control of most of northern Iraq from a rival Kurdish faction at the end of last month. The Iraqi intervention prompted U.S. missile strikes on Iraq Sept. 3 and 4.
Although the U.S. statement did not say so, a prime message that Washington has wanted to deliver to Barzani is that he should abandon his alliance with Baghdad.
